hero.eyebrow: Presentation skills · No software to install
hero.title: PowerPoint Presentation Design: learn by doing
hero.subtitle: Plan, build and deliver talks in a working slide studio inside your browser. Every deck is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can build a clear, persuasive deck and deliver it with confidence.

outcomes.title: Plan the message
outcomes.text: Audience, purpose, a one-sentence message and a storyboard.

outcomes.title: Write words that work
outcomes.text: Headlines that make a point and slides that can be read in seconds.

outcomes.title: Show data honestly
outcomes.text: Diagrams, shapes and charts that are clean and fair.

outcomes.title: Tell the story
outcomes.text: Openings, signposts, rehearsal and handling questions.

outcomes.title: Finish professionally
outcomes.text: A review checklist, accessible files and strong delivery online or in a room.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the final talk and the final assessment.

faq.a: No. The slide studio runs in your browser. The ideas carry over to PowerPoint, Google Slides, Keynote and Canva.
About six and a half hours, in short sessions.

faq.q: Will my deck be judged on taste?
faq.a: The checks look at structure: titles, readability, layout variety, shapes and key content. Taste is yours.

activities.title: Introduce yourself in five slides
activities.objective: Build a short, readable deck with a title slide and clear slide titles.
activities.scenario: Your class is meeting new people. Make five short slides so they can get to know you.
steps: Make slide 1 a Title slide with your name.
Add four more slides titled About me, My hobbies, My goals and Thank you.
Write two or three short bullet points on each content slide.
Choose a theme other than the default.

checks.label: Five to seven slides
checks.hint: Use Add slide to make more.
checks.explain: Five slides are enough to introduce yourself without losing people.

checks.label: A title slide first
checks.hint: Choose the Title slide layout for slide 1 and type your name.
checks.explain: The first slide introduces the talk.

checks.label: Every slide has a title
checks.hint: Type a title at the top of each slide.
checks.explain: Titles tell the audience what each slide is about.

checks.label: A slide about your hobbies
checks.hint: Make a slide title or text include Hobbies.
checks.explain: Hobbies give the audience something to connect with.

checks.label: A slide about your goals
checks.hint: Make a slide title or text include Goals.
checks.explain: Goals tell people where you are heading.

checks.label: Few words per slide
checks.hint: Keep to four bullets and about 30 words.
checks.explain: Slides support what you say; they are not a script.

checks.label: A theme other than the default
checks.hint: Open the theme list and pick one.
checks.explain: A theme gives the deck a consistent look.

activities.title: Rescue an overloaded slide
activities.objective: Turn a wall of text into slides people can read while you speak.
activities.scenario: A student wrote everything on one slide. Split it into clear slides with at most four short bullets each.
steps: Keep slide 1 as the title slide.
Split the long slide into at least three slides, each with its own clear title.
Reduce every slide to four bullets or fewer, with about 25 words or fewer.
Add a final slide that says what you want the audience to do.

checks.label: At least five slides in total
checks.hint: Move the points onto several new slides.
checks.explain: One idea per slide is easier to follow.

checks.label: Every slide has a title
checks.hint: Give each new slide a title that says what it is about.
checks.explain: A good title tells the audience the point of the slide.

checks.label: No slide has more than four bullets or about 25 words
checks.hint: Cut each bullet down to its key words.
checks.explain: People cannot read and listen at the same time.

checks.label: The first slide is still the title slide
checks.hint: Do not lose the title slide.
checks.explain: The talk starts with a title.

checks.label: A closing slide with a call to action
checks.hint: Add a slide whose text includes Next steps or Please.
checks.explain: End by telling people what to do next.

slides.title: Everything about recycling
slides.body:
- Recycling is the process of converting waste materials into new materials and objects, which can reduce the use of fresh raw materials
- Paper, plastic, glass and metal can all be recycled in different ways depending on the facilities available in the town
- Our school produces about forty kilograms of waste every day, and most of it ends up in a single large bin
- We measured the waste for two weeks and wrote everything down in a long table that we will not show here
- Many students did not know which bin to use
- The municipal truck comes twice a week
- We think we can do better
- Thank you for listening

activities.title: Add a diagram and a bold look
activities.objective: Use shapes to show a process, and keep layouts varied but consistent.
activities.scenario: Explain how a school canteen order moves from the student to the kitchen, using shapes to draw the steps.
steps: Make slide 1 a Title slide: Canteen orders.
Add a Section slide called The journey.
Add a Title and bullets slide, then add at least three shapes (boxes and an arrow) to draw the steps: Order, Cook, Collect.
Add a Two columns slide comparing Before and After.
Pick a theme other than the default.

checks.label: A title slide first
checks.hint: Choose the Title slide layout and type Canteen orders.
checks.explain: Start with a clear title.

checks.label: At least three different layouts
checks.hint: Use a title, a section and a two-column slide.
checks.explain: Different layouts keep a deck from looking monotonous.

checks.label: At least three shapes to draw the steps
checks.hint: Use the Shape button for boxes and an arrow.
checks.explain: A simple diagram can replace a paragraph.

checks.label: The steps Order, Cook and Collect appear
checks.hint: Write the three step names on the slide.
checks.explain: Name each step so the diagram is understood.

checks.label: A non-default theme
checks.hint: Pick a theme from the list.
checks.explain: A theme keeps fonts and colours consistent.

checks.label: Every slide has a title
checks.hint: Give each slide a title.
checks.explain: Titles help the audience keep track.

activities.title: Tell a story in seven slides
activities.objective: Give a talk a beginning, middle and end, with one idea per slide and a strong close.
activities.scenario: You must persuade the principal to start a morning reading half hour. Build the deck.
steps: Slide 1: a Title slide with a clear title.
Slide 2: the problem. Slide 3: evidence. Slide 4: your idea.
Slides 5 and 6: benefits and cost.
Slide 7: a clear request, titled Our request.
Keep every slide to four bullets or fewer.

checks.label: Six to eight slides
checks.hint: Plan the story before you type.
checks.explain: A short deck keeps attention.

checks.label: A title slide first
checks.hint: Choose the Title layout for slide 1.
checks.explain: The first slide frames the talk.

checks.label: Every slide has a title
checks.hint: A title for each slide.
checks.explain: Titles carry the story if someone only reads the headlines.

checks.label: A slide about the problem
checks.hint: Include the word problem on a slide.
checks.explain: Say what is wrong before you offer a fix.

checks.label: A final request slide
checks.hint: Include Our request on the last slide.
checks.explain: End with a specific ask.

checks.label: Readable slides
checks.hint: Four bullets and about 30 words or fewer per slide.
checks.explain: People should read each slide in seconds.

activities.title: Final project: a ten-minute talk
activities.objective: Bring structure, readable slides, visuals and a strong close together.
activities.scenario: Present a plan to improve something at your school or in your community. Build a deck of seven to nine slides.
steps: Slide 1: a Title slide naming your plan.
Include a slide called The problem and a slide called Our plan.
Draw one simple diagram with at least three shapes.
Use at least three different layouts.
Keep every slide to four bullets or fewer and about 30 words.
Finish with a slide titled Next steps.

checks.label: Seven to nine slides
checks.hint: Plan the talk before you type.
checks.explain: A ten-minute talk needs about eight slides.

checks.label: A title slide first
checks.hint: Choose the Title layout.
checks.explain: The deck opens with its title.

checks.label: Every slide has a title
checks.hint: Check each slide.
checks.explain: Titles carry the structure.

checks.label: A slide called The problem
checks.hint: Include The problem as a title.
checks.explain: State the problem before the plan.

checks.label: A slide called Our plan
checks.hint: Include Our plan as a title.
checks.explain: Say clearly what you propose.

checks.label: A diagram with at least three shapes
checks.hint: Use the Shape button on one slide.
checks.explain: A simple diagram helps people see the process.

checks.label: At least three layouts
checks.hint: Use title, bullets and two-column layouts.
checks.explain: Variety keeps the audience interested.

checks.label: Readable slides
checks.hint: Four bullets and about 30 words or fewer per slide.
checks.explain: Each slide should be read in seconds.

checks.hint: End with Next steps.
